mainEntity.name: Can a veneer fall off completely, and what should I do if it does?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is possible for a veneer to become fully debonded and detach from the tooth. If this happens, try to keep the veneer in a safe place and contact your dental practice as soon as possible to arrange an assessment. Avoid attempting to reattach it yourself. The dentist will evaluate the tooth and the veneer to determine whether rebonding is possible or whether a replacement is required. This depends on the condition of both the tooth and the veneer itself.

mainEntity.name: Is sensitivity after getting veneers placed normal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some degree of sensitivity in the days or weeks following veneer placement is not uncommon, as the tooth adjusts to the new restoration. This typically settles on its own. However, if sensitivity persists beyond a few weeks, worsens over time, or returns after having settled, it is worth bringing this to your dentist's attention. Persistent sensitivity may indicate that further assessment is needed to check the tooth and bonding.

mainEntity.name: Can decay develop under a veneer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, decay can develop beneath or around the margin of a veneer, particularly if oral hygiene is not consistently maintained or if the bonding seal has degraded over time. This is one of the key reasons why regular dental check-ups are recommended for patients with veneers. Early-stage decay may not cause obvious symptoms, so professional monitoring allows issues to be identified and addressed before they become more complex.

mainEntity.name: Do veneers require any special cleaning products?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, standard brushing with a non-abrasive fluoride toothpaste and a soft-bristled toothbrush is appropriate. Highly abrasive toothpastes or whitening toothpastes with coarse particles are generally best avoided, as they can scratch porcelain surfaces over time. Your dental team can offer personalised product recommendations based on the type of veneers you have and your individual oral health needs.

mainEntity.name: Can veneers be repaired, or do they always need to be replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether a damaged veneer can be repaired or needs to be replaced depends on the nature and extent of the damage. Small chips to composite veneers can sometimes be repaired directly at the chairside. Porcelain veneers, however, are more difficult to repair due to the nature of the material, and replacement may be required in some cases. A clinical assessment is needed to determine the most appropriate option for each individual situation.

mainEntity.name: How often should I attend dental check-ups if I have veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most patients, attending dental check-ups every six to twelve months is a reasonable general guideline, though your dentist may recommend a different frequency based on your individual oral health needs. Patients with veneers benefit particularly from consistent check-up attendance, as this allows the dentist to monitor veneer condition, check surrounding gum and tooth health, and offer timely guidance if any changes are noted.
